name: Carbon Emissions and Large Neural Network Training
problem: ML compute demand has grown fast with real energy and carbon costs, but energy use is hard to estimate without detailed information, so the cost is invisible and the optimisation target is undefined.
mechanism: Measurement methodology plus sensitivity analysis rather than an optimisation algorithm: compute energy use and carbon footprint for several large models (T5, Meena, GShard, Switch Transformer, GPT-3), refine earlier estimates for the evolved transformer architecture search, and attribute the totals to the individual choices of DNN architecture, datacenter location, time-of-day, and processor type.
speedup_reported: Not a speedup paper. The reportable findings, each with its own baseline: large but SPARSELY ACTIVATED DNNs can consume LESS THAN 1/10TH the energy of large dense DNNs without sacrificing accuracy, despite using as many or more parameters; geographic location matters because the carbon-free fraction and resulting CO2e vary ~5X-10X even within the same country and the same organization; cloud datacenters are ~1.4-2X more energy efficient than typical datacenters, and ML-oriented accelerators inside them are ~2-5X more effective than off-the-shelf systems; and the COMBINED choice of DNN, datacenter, and processor can reduce the carbon footprint up to ~100-1000X.
notes: ADOPTION: in-production as a REPORTING STANDARD rather than a technique - the authors state they are collaborating with MLPerf developers to include energy usage during training AND inference in that industry-standard benchmark, which is why this 2021 paper is still the citation for energy-per-model figures. VENUE NOTE: no peer-reviewed venue verifiable via Semantic Scholar at verification time (rate-limited) and the arXiv comment carries no venue, so venue = arxiv-preprint, year = ArXiv v1 (Apr 2021). THE NUMBER TO CARRY FORWARD IS THE ~100-1000X SPREAD: the authors use it to argue that retroactive energy estimates are difficult and error-prone, which is the honest framing - a single carbon figure for a model is meaningless without the datacenter, region, time, and hardware recorded alongside it. Note also that the 1/10th-energy sparse-activation result is the origin of the sparsity-is-a-carbon-intervention argument that later work on MoE serving builds on.
